validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE/ATTRIBUTION all check out. This is a real, FERC-docketed FGT mainline compressor uprate, NOT a GEM-only entity: Federal Register 86 FR 63008 (FR doc 2021-24831, published 2021-11-15) states FGT filed a prior-notice request on Oct 28, 2021 in Docket No. CP22-12-000 'for authorization to increase mainline capacity, and make minor auxiliary facility modifications ... on compressor units 1007 and 1008 at Compressor Station 10 (CS 10) in Perry County, Mississippi,' to 'transport incremental interstate gas from an existing receipt point in George County, Mississippi, to three existing delivery points in Mobile County, Alabama.' EIA's Aug-2026 Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (Historical Projects sheet, row 1058) carries the same project under docket CP22-12, operator 'Florida Gas Trans Co', States MS/AL, Status Completed, in-service 2022 -- one origin (EIA) but it corroborates the FERC filing's own facts (docket, states, scope) as an independent second origin. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a transmission mainline project (FERC explicitly calls it 'mainline capacity'; Kinder Morgan's current FGT overview page (kindermorgan.com/business/gas_pipelines/east/FGT, live 2026-09) describes FGT as an operating 'approximately 5,400-mile system that transports natural gas from South Texas to South Florida,' operated by Energy Transfer, owned by Florida Gas Transmission Company LLC (100% subsidiary of Citrus Corp, a 50/50 Kinder Morgan/Energy Transfer JV) -- confirms Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission, Owner1/Owner1%, and that FGT continues to operate today. DUPLICATE: no other roster row describes this project; P5548 (South Louisiana Project) and P7824 (South Central Louisiana, batch A1) are FGT siblings but distinct dockets/scopes -- see cross_row_leads for a CS10-related lead on P5548. SCOPE: LengthKnown=0.00 mi / Diameter blank is CORRECT per the compression-only rule -- FERC's notice describes only compressor-unit and 'minor auxiliary facility' work at an existing station, no new pipe or looping, so LengthKnown=0 is confirmed, not a defect. The Kinder Morgan FGT page (kindermorgan.com/pages/business/gas_pipelines/east/FGT/default.aspx) cited on the gem.wiki page is now a 404 -- dead, superseded by kindermorgan.com/business/gas_pipelines/east/FGT (used here). The bit.ly/2smVBv2 wiki citation resolves to abarrelfull.wikidot.com (A Barrel Full) -- BANNED, not opened/used.

validity.recommendation: Verify Capacity against FGT's actual CP22-12 application/exhibits (FERC eLibrary, JS-walled to script access) before treating 175 MMcf/d as settled -- the only primary regulatory document found states an order of magnitude less.
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity disagreement between the sheet/EIA and the primary FERC filing. The sheet records Capacity=175.00 MMcf/d, and EIA's Aug-2026 workbook (Historical Projects row 1058) agrees exactly (Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) = 175) -- but EIA's own number is very likely transcribed from the same FERC prior-notice filing, and that filing (Federal Register 86 FR 63008 / FR doc 2021-24831, Docket CP22-12-000) states the project 'is designed primarily to meet the demand for an additional 17,500 million British Thermal Units per day (MMBtu/d)' -- confirmed against the original govinfo.gov scanned PDF (FR-2021-11-15/pdf/2021-24831.pdf), not an OCR artifact. At natural gas's standard heat content (~1.03 MMBtu/Mcf), 17,500 MMBtu/d is approximately 17 MMcf/d -- roughly 1/10th of the recorded/EIA 175 MMcf/d, and the ratio is exactly 10x, which reads like a dropped/added zero somewhere in the chain (either in FGT's original application, in FERC's Federal Register summary of it, or in EIA's transcription) rather than two genuinely different figures. I could not reach FERC eLibrary's docket sheet for CP22-12 to see the actual application exhibits or confirm which number is final (elibrary.ferc.gov is an Angular SPA; docket-number search returns no server-side-renderable result to script access) -- searched Federal Register, govinfo.gov, and general web search for a superseding FERC order or amendment to CP22-12 and found none (this is a 'prior notice' under FGT's blanket certificate, which is deemed authorized without a published order if unprotested, so no confirming order is expected in the Federal Register). Leaving `contested.Capacity` blank rather than asserting a specific replacement number, since I cannot confirm whether 17,500 MMBtu/d was the FINAL authorized/built capacity or an earlier target that grew before completion. Do not paste over 175 without a human pulling the actual CP22-12 application from eLibrary.
